newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African growers see another bumper sugar crop.
newsitem.headline: S.African growers see another bumper sugar crop.

text.p: South Africa is line for another bumper sugar crop this season with production in 1997/98 (April-March) seen as high as 2.5 million tonnes, said the chairman of the country's Cane Growers Association at the organisation's annual meeting on Tuesday.
South Africa harvested its first good sugar cane after five years of drought last year, yielding 2.27 million tonnes of raw sugar, leaving around one million tonnes for export.
But Stewart cautioned that this year the focus would be on the recovery of the industry.
"While the improvement in the crop enables growers to enhance their situation, to overcome the legacy of debt will require continuing favourable weather and good management."
The availability of additional sugar would enable the industry to take advantage of the broader overseas marketing opportunities that exist for South African producers, he said.

"The price earned for our sucrose is largely dependent on the level of sugar sales achieved in the Southern African Customs Union market, which has grown by 2.75 percent per annum over the last 10 years," Stewart said.
He added that early predictions for South African sugar's 1997/98 share of the Customs Union market was about 80 percent. In 1994 South Africa held about 93 percent of the market share.

"The need to secure our domestic market as well as a reasonable share of the markets of non sugar producing members of the Customs Union is of crucial importance to the long-term survival of our industry," Stewart said.
